messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A familiar inventory routine; then one item behaves strangely halfway through the routine. Practicality says leave it while instinct says keep it. What happens next?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "i keep the old item, then i move it to the floor and put it on the shelf. “i did not leave it,” i say. “i kept it because i was younger and more curious.” the shelf clicks, and i move the item again. “i left it,” i say. “i kept it because i was younger and more curious.” the memory clicks."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "Leave it. I put it down. The watch ticks. I move it to the drawer. The drawer is empty. I put the second item back. The routine is not finished. I keep the first item."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "I mark the misplaced shaft with grease and leave it halfway. I run one shorter version, then leave the original routine alone. I keep the scratched shaft beside the broken one."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "I keep the old item beside the new one. I tap the shelf with my heel, then put the old one back on the bench. I fold the old one in half and test the middle with my thumb, but the joint slips. I leave it on the shelf and count the old one twice."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "i leave the worn item aside and tap the cover once. if it stays, i keep the old routine; if it moves, i mark the new spot with grease."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "Left one. Right one."}, {"id": "R019", "response": "I scrape the rust from the bench edge once. \"Leave it,\" I say. I take the rust and leave it halfway. I mark the joint with my thumbnail. \"Leave it.\" I leave it there."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "i put the item in the corner and wait. i touch the edge with my thumbnail, but the wrapper stays open. i put it back in the same spot, then leave it beside the forgotten one. the wrapper stays open, so i write \"keep\" beside it."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "you put the familiar in the corner. “not the same.” you turn the item once. “you leave.” the routine repeats. you keep the strange one. the corner is empty. you leave the familiar. the second item stays."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "I put the last thing I bought on the bench. the dust catches the paper, then leaves a small mark. I leave the other thing beside it. the routine stays. the piece can come back later."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "\"One. half. It stays. Likely.\" I check the watch, then the order. \"Maybe wrong.\" I leave the item, but I keep it tidy."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "i put the dirty sock on the table and wait. the shoe clicks once, then stops. i leave it that way. the inventory has three choices: leave, hold the sock, or keep the sock. the sock has been here twice, so i decide the third choice feels fair. i fold one card into a small square, then leave it. the inventory has moved one item."}]
